html:
El Dorado, the golden one, was the Spanish name for a ruler of the Muisca people of the Colombian highlands who was said to cover himself in gold dust and plunge into Lake Guatavita. The tale became the legend of a lost city of gold.

The Muisca lived around today's Bogotá, farming, mining salt and trading for gold, which their smiths worked into offerings. A gold raft found in 1969 shows the ceremony: a ruler with his attendants on a raft on the lake. Spanish soldiers under Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada conquered the Muisca in 1537 and 1538.

The legend grew as it travelled. For a century expeditions searched for El Dorado across the Andes, the Orinoco and the Amazon, among them the German governors of Venezuela and Walter Raleigh. Attempts to drain Lake Guatavita for treasure failed. Many pieces now sit in the Gold Museum of Colombia.
